title: Spiderman Brand New Day
description: Reviewers say 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' showcases Tom Holland's strongest performance yet, supported by stunning cinematography and Destin Daniel Cretton's masterful direction. Sadie Sink steals scenes while the film delivers breathtaking action and genuine emotional depth. However, pacing issues plague the lengthy runtime, and the writing receives mixed reactions for conventional plotting and weak villain development. Despite structural weaknesses, the character-driven story successfully matures Peter Parker into a vulnerable, relatable hero.

title: Project Hail Mary
description: Reviewers say 'Project Hail Mary' delivers stunning cinematography and exceptional performances, particularly Ryan Gosling's career-best work. The film's emotional core—an authentic friendship—resonates deeply, blending humor with heartfelt moments. However, pacing proves divisive, with some finding the slow start tedious while others appreciate the deliberate rhythm. Scientific depth polarizes audiences, balancing accessibility against the book's complexity. Despite mixed reactions to engagement levels and runtime, most find it a visually spectacular, emotionally moving adaptation that successfully translates Andy Weir's novel to screen.

title: Mental Health First Aid (Student)
description: MHFA is an 8-hour training is a national public education program that introduces participants to risk factors and warning signs of mental illnesses and substance use, builds understanding of their impact, and overviews common supports. This course demonstrates how to offer initial help in a mental health crisis and connect persons to the appropriate professional, peer, social, and self-help care. The program also teaches the common risk factors and warning signs of specific types of illnesses like anxiety, depression, substance use disorder, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia. The training is both educational and experiential and includes: An overview of statistics regarding mental health and suicide Myths versus facts Behavioral, verbal, and situational warning signs Concrete tools for helping someone in distress REGISTRATION REQUIRED. Each session has a maximum of 30 participants and a minimum of 5.To register for these sessions, please log in to the Learning & Development portal . *** Participants must complete 2 hours of pre-work and attend the full 6 hours of the instructor led training to earn their certificate. For questions about Mental Health First Aid Training, please contact suicideprevention@charlotte.edu .

title: Mental Health First Aid (Student)
description: MHFA is an 8-hour training is a national public education program that introduces participants to risk factors and warning signs of mental illnesses and substance use, builds understanding of their impact, and overviews common supports. This course demonstrates how to offer initial help in a mental health crisis and connect persons to the appropriate professional, peer, social, and self-help care. The program also teaches the common risk factors and warning signs of specific types of illnesses like anxiety, depression, substance use disorder, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia. The training is both educational and experiential and includes: An overview of statistics regarding mental health and suicide Myths versus facts Behavioral, verbal, and situational warning signs Concrete tools for helping someone in distress REGISTRATION REQUIRED. Each session has a maximum of 30 participants and a minimum of 5.To register for these sessions, please log in to the Learning & Development portal . *** Participants must complete 2 hours of pre-work and attend the full 6 hours of the instructor led training to earn their certificate. For questions about Mental Health First Aid Training, please contact suicideprevention@charlotte.edu .

title: Mental Health First Aid (Faculty and Staff) (Cancelled)
description: MHFA is an 8-hour training is a national public education program that introduces participants to risk factors and warning signs of mental illnesses and substance use, builds understanding of their impact, and overviews common supports. This course demonstrates how to offer initial help in a mental health crisis and connect persons to the appropriate professional, peer, social, and self-help care. The program also teaches the common risk factors and warning signs of specific types of illnesses like anxiety, depression, substance use disorder, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia. The training is both educational and experiential and includes: An overview of statistics regarding mental health and suicide Myths versus facts Behavioral, verbal, and situational warning signs Concrete tools for helping someone in distress REGISTRATION REQUIRED. Each session has a maximum of 30 participants and a minimum of 5.To register for these sessions, please log in to the Learning & Development portal . *** Participants must complete 2 hours of pre-work and attend the full 6 hours of the instructor led training to earn their certificate. For questions about Mental Health First Aid Training, please contact suicideprevention@charlotte.edu .
